body:
- **Data centres:** India had about 1.8 GW IT of operational DC stock in H1 2026, after adding 258 MW in H1 2026 (Savills). Forecasts for 2030 are 6–8 GW (Jefferies: 8 GW). Hyperscaler commitments include Google/AdaniConneX Vizag (about $15bn, 2026–30), Microsoft ($17.5bn) and AWS (figures conflict). Each GW of DC load needs EHV substations, transformers, switchgear, gensets, cooling and BESS.
- **Grid:** Peak demand hit a record **270.8 GW on 21 May 2026** (MoP data, via DownToEarth/PolicyCircle). T&D capex is put at about ₹9 trn to 2032 (April 2026 report), and ICRA estimates ₹5.6 trn of transmission capex FY27–32. About 56,000 ckm and 338 GVA were under construction through FY30 (Mercom, June 2026). Transformer lead times are long and pricing has been firm (April 2026 report).
- **Storage:** 100+ GWh of BESS was tendered in 2025 (IESA; counts conflict between 58.7 and 102 GWh). Operational BESS was only about 9 GWh by Aug 2026, so execution is lagging tenders.

**Thesis in one line:** the demand side is real and dated. **But the obvious "shortage" trade (transformer OEMs) is already showing peak-margin behaviour.** Shilchar, Voltamp, Indo Tech and Vilas Transcore have all printed 3–4 consecutive quarters of falling OPM while everyone adds capacity. The less-crowded trade is **transmission EPC and towers**, where order books are 1.8–1.9x revenue and P/Es are 14–24x. Capital goods took 14 years to regain the 2007 peak, so I did not pay 50–80x for anything.

Sources: [Savills via RealtyToday](https://therealtytoday.com/news/market-insights/indias-data-centre-infrastructure-reaches-18-gw-with-rising-global-investments-savills-india-report/), [CXO Digital Pulse 6–8 GW](https://www.cxodigitalpulse.com/?p=64062), [Google Vizag](https://www.pulse.bot/climatetech/news/google-clouds-planned-15-billion-data-centre-in-visakhapatnam-to-have-5-gw-capacity-ca9a7383-3e0d-4c48-955d-a505db15e623/), [270.8 GW peak – DownToEarth](https://www.downtoearth.org.in/amp/story/energy/power-demand-tracker-india-meets-all-time-high-power-demand-of-2708-gw-renewable-energy-share-34), [₹9 trn T&D capex](https://www.ibef.org/news/india-s-power-transmission-sector-to-see-us-96-70-billion-capex-push-by-2032), [ICRA ₹5.6 trn](https://www.energetica-india.net/news/transmission-sector-to-witness-inr-56-trillion-capex-between-202627-and-203132-says-icra), [Mercom build-out](https://mercomindia.com/clean-energy-expansion-spurs-transmission-manufacturing-demand), [BESS tenders – SaurEnergy](https://www.saurenergy.com/solar-energy-news/indias-ess-shift-92-gwh-set-for-commissions-in-2026-after-130-gwh-of-tenders-in-2025-10993901)

`person:howard-marks` | confidence: **verified** | tags: us, global, process, credit, base-rate, avoid-ruin

Co-founder of Oaktree Capital (1995); memos since 1990 (the Jan 2000 'bubble.com' memo called the tech top); books The Most Important Thing (2011) and Mastering the Market Cycle (2018). Structural edge: a credit/distressed-debt franchise with locked-up capital that can deploy when others must sell. Signature trade: in 2008 Oaktree raised $10.9bn for OCM Opportunities Fund VIIb - its largest distressed fund, 3x the previous one - began investing in May 2008 and deployed most of it between Lehman's bankruptcy and year-end 2008 (reportedly ~$500m a week), targeting 25-30%+ gross; by 2011 it had returned $3bn to LPs (final realised IRR not found). Process: 'second-level thinking' (what is priced in, not just what is good); 'you can't predict, you can prepare' - take the market's temperature (credit spreads, issuance quality, investor attitudes, 'too good to be true' deals) and lean aggressive when fear is high and defensive when risk appetite is high; winning by avoiding losers. Mistakes: his cautious memos were early in several long bull runs (e.g., 2017-2021) - temperature reading gives direction, not timing. Copyable: build a simple 'market temperature' checklist for India (smallcap-to-Nifty P/E premium, IPO/SME subscription multiples, F&O retail volumes, market cap/GDP, credit spreads) and adjust equity allocation in steps rather than going all-in or all-out.

| copyable | temperature checklist, stepwise allocation |
| mistakes | early caution in long bull runs |

- **2 70/20/10 yearly: PASS** (DD −17.0pp; CAGR +0.80pp; worst 5-yr +5.4pp). Survives the gold-at-7% sensitivity (−16.1pp,
  −0.38pp). Fails the 15pp gate if you start after the 2008 crash (−10.8pp) — the benefit is concentrated in rare crashes.
- **3 ±5pp bands: PASS** (−16.3pp, +0.73pp), but no better than yearly → no reason to prefer it.
- **6 50/50 equity/gold: PASS** (−28.2pp, +1.92pp) — the most gold-dependent: with gold at 7% the CAGR cost is 1.07pp → fails.
- **4 P/E tilt: literal PASS** on the extra rule (DD −15.1% beats 70/20/10's −18.6%), **but not adopted:** CAGR is lower than
  both alternatives, a fixed split at its own average equity weight (66.9%) gets −17.5% DD at +0.49pp more CAGR, the
  remaining edge rests on one episode (Mar-2020, when it sat at 60%), the window has ~2 independent 5-yr periods, and P/E showed
  no out-of-sample power in L51. Lesson for future rules: a timing rule must beat a fixed split *at the same average weight*.
- **5 new money to most-underweight: PASS** its rule (XIRR 11.30% vs 11.06% for SIP + yearly reset; tax 0 vs ₹2.47L). Part of
  the gain is that it drifted to 31% gold during a gold boom; once the pot is large, contributions cannot hold the targets.
- Caveats as pre-stated: rupee depreciation (−3.7%/yr) and a record gold run (+72% in 2025) flatter gold; tax simplified
  (debt-fund gains after Apr-2023 are slab-taxed, gold/bond 20% used throughout; equity 10%/12.5% with no ₹1–1.25L exemption);
  fund NAVs carry regular-plan fees (direct plans would add ~0.5–1pp to equity and bonds).

**Confidence:** `single-source` overall — gold and bonds are cross-checked (verified), equity uses one fund series with index
checks, P/E tilt is `unverified` (13-yr window).

- **M1 = L2-penalised logistic regression**, intercept unpenalised, prior N(0, 1) on each coefficient (penalty ½β²),
  training weights normalised to mean 1, fitted by Newton's method on the training fold only. Prediction clipped to
  [0.02, 0.60]. (Base rate × likelihood ratios was considered and rejected as primary: the flags are correlated, so
  multiplying LRs double-counts.)
- **B = class base rate alone** = weighted blow-up rate of the training fold (same for every firm in the test fold).
- **Card comparators** (scenario blow-up p = 0.05, the L48 card-shaped set, anchor weight 0.5):
  C0 = current v1.5 anchoring = 0.5·B + 0.5·0.05; **C1a** = 0.5·B + 0.5·max(0.05, M1) (model replaces the scenario p,
  anchoring kept); **C1b** = max(C0, M1) (model as a floor on the anchored value); C2 = max(C0, B) (base-rate floor).
- **Split:** leave-one-cohort-out within each panel (primary). **By market (secondary, reported):** coefficients of
  {S1, S2, S5} fitted on all US rows, applied to India non-fin with the intercept re-set so the mean prediction on the
  India training fold equals its B; scored on the India held-out fold.
